B1a.claim: Any J = M⁻¹K with K antisymmetric satisfies JᵀM + MJ = 0

B1b.claim: Elliptic case (det M > 0): A(s) = cos s·I + sin s·J has AᵀMA = M

B1c.claim: Hyperbolic case (det M < 0): A(s) = cosh s·I + sinh s·J has AᵀMA = M

B1d.claim: Null vectors are η-orthogonal to themselves: (1,1)ᵀη(1,1) = 0

B2a.claim: Residual of the G-projection is G-orthogonal: uᵀG(v − (uᵀGv / uᵀGu)u) = 0

B2b.claim: ∇(xᵀGx) = 2Gx, so the tangent plane of the unit ball at û has normal Gu

B3a.claim: Over one period [0, 2π], {cos kt, sin kt}ₖ₌₁³ has Gram matrix π·I

B3b.claim: Closed form used live: ∫₀ᴸ cos t·cos 3t dt = ½(sin 2L/2 + sin 4L/4)

B4a.claim: Parseval for a 3-harmonic trig sum: ∫₀^{2π} x² dt = π Σ(aₖ² + bₖ²)

B4b.claim: On any interval: ‖x₁+x₂‖² = ‖x₁‖² + ‖x₂‖² + 2⟨x₁,x₂⟩; the cross term is 0 at L = 2π

B5a.claim: Time-average ⟨cos(ωt+φ), cos(ω(t+τ)+φ)⟩ = ½cos ωτ, independent of φ

B5a2.claim: [added after B5a FAILED] time-average ⟨cos(ωt+φ), cos(ω(t+τ)+φ)⟩ = ½cos ωτ, independent of φ

B5c.claim: r = p/q ⇒ D(2πq) = 0 exactly (a true symmetry of the shifted signal)

B6a.claim: The 24 signed permutation matrices with det +1 form a group (closed under products)

B7a.claim: The cyclic shift (x₁,x₂,x₃) ↦ (x₃,x₁,x₂) equals the 120° rotation about (1,1,1)

B7b.claim: P = (I + S + S²)/3 is the orthogonal projector onto span(1,1,1): P² = P, Pᵀ = P

C1a.claim: antisymmetric J (2x2): x^T J x = 0 for all real x

C1a(2).claim: antisymmetric J (4x4): x^T J x = 0 for all real x

C1b.claim: (A^T M A)_ij = B(A e_i, A e_j) for general 2x2 A, M  (so A^T M A = M is form preservation)

C1c.claim: diag(2,1) keeps x^T J x = 0 yet D^T J D = 2J != J; the Hamiltonian flow exp(sK) of S9 keeps A^T J A = J

C2a.claim: symmetric M: K^T M + M K is symmetric, so conservation of z^T M z <=> K^T M + M K = 0; antisymmetric J: K = I conserves z^T J z trivially but K^T J + J K = 2J

C8a.claim: wrapping: |e^{iwt}| = 1 for all t, and lim_{t->oo} cos(wt) does not exist (AccumBounds(-1,1))

C8b.claim: compressing: theta in (0,oo) -> e^{-theta t_i} in (0,1); theta->0+ gives (1,1,1), theta->oo gives (0,0,0)

C8c.claim: square wave: ||S_N - f||_2 shrinks (ratio 0.109 < 0.05) but max S_N stays > 1.17 (1.1813, 1.1790, 1.1790)

C8c2.claim: square wave: RMS error equals the Parseval tail (rel. err 0.0008 < 0.01) and the tail -> 0; overshoot persists (max S_N > 1.17)

C8d.claim: quasi-periodic: no exact return (sqrt2 irrational) but near-returns D(2pi q) = [0.9291, 0.2635, 0.049, 0.0085, 0.0015]

C9a.claim: Lambda_c^T M_c Lambda_c = M_c with M_c = diag(1, -1/c^2)  [S5c in matrix form]

C9b.claim: c -> oo: M_c -> diag(1, 0), det M_c = -1/c^2 -> 0  (the form degenerates: only time is measured)

C9c.claim: boost generator K_c = [[0,-1/c^2],[-1,0]]: det K_c = -1/c^2 < 0 (hyperbolic); K_oo = [[0,0],[-1,0]], K_oo^2 = 0 (shear)

C9d.claim: Galilean boost exp(v K_oo) = [[1,0],[-v,1]] preserves the degenerate form diag(1,0)

O1a.claim: Rodrigues rotation about any unit axis: R^T R = I, hence (Ru).(Rv) = u.v

O1b.claim: orthogonal (1,0,0),(0,1,0) seen along (1,1,1) appear at 120 deg; (1,0,1),(0,1,1) at 60 deg appear at 90 deg from above

O1c.claim: sampled cosines on N = 8 and N = 12 points: sum cos(2pi m j/N)cos(2pi n j/N) = (N/2) delta_mn for m + n < N

O1d.claim: left Riemann sums approach the integral off-period: errors (N=64, N=1024) = [(0.04991, 0.003113), (0.0045, 0.000371)]

O1e.claim: with unit e1=(1,0), e2=(cos t, sin t): Parseval gap is 0 for all x only at t = pi/2; reconstruction exact there, not at t = pi/3

S3.claim: T_tau e_k = exp(-2 pi i k tau) e_k

S4e.claim: rotation preserves x^2+y^2 for all s

S4f.claim: boost preserves x^2-y^2 for all s

S5d.claim: c -> inf: (x', t') -> (x - v t, t)  [Galilean]
